result.title: TAPES: Task-Aligned Joint Predictive Pretraining for Transaction Event Sequences
result.summary: Transaction event sequences support diverse prediction tasks in online commerce and digital financial services. The same transaction records can yield prediction targets with different semantics, including values, changes, and relations to past events. These targets impose different constraints on history representations, but their predictability alone does not establish the downstream utility of a target set. Moreover, target-wise prediction losses do not explicitly model conditional co-occurrence among targets. To address these challenges, we propose TAPES, a task-aligned joint predictive pretraining framework for transaction sequences. TAPES constructs a finite collection of candidate target sets from admissible field-operator combinations. It selects a target set according to the downstream utility of representations learned through short joint pretraining trials under matched budgets. It then reinitializes the encoder and pretrains it on the selected targets through a joint likelihood parameterized by a shared discrete latent variable, before downstream supervised adaptation. Experiments in a real-world transaction-risk setting and on multiple public financial benchmarks spanning diverse downstream tasks demonstrate that TAPES outperforms representative baselines. Ablation studies further validate the contributions of predictive target selection and joint modeling.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TAPES 框架，用于交易事件序列的预训练：从字段—算子组合构造候选预测目标集，按短程联合预训练后的下游效用挑选目标集，再以共享离散隐变量参数化的联合似然预训练编码器，最后进行下游监督适配。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按下游效用筛选预测目标集」与「共享离散隐变量联合建模目标间条件共现」的监督分配思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中哪些 latent 预测目标值得训练、目标间依赖如何建模；但论文本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理。
